source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 10.

sections.heading: 1. Reflection and Mirrors
points: **Light travels in a straight line** and **reflects** off shiny surfaces.
**Laws of reflection:** angle of incidence = angle of reflection; incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane.
A **plane mirror** gives a **virtual, erect, laterally inverted** image of the same size.

sections.heading: 2. Spherical Mirrors
points: **Concave mirror** — curves **inward**, **converges** light; can give real or virtual, magnified images.
Uses of concave mirror: **shaving/make-up mirror, dentist's mirror, torch and headlight reflectors, solar cooker**.
**Convex mirror** — curves **outward**, **diverges** light; always gives a **small, virtual, erect** image with a **wide field of view**.
Uses of convex mirror: **rear-view (side) mirrors** in vehicles.

sections.heading: 3. Lenses
points: **Convex (converging) lens** — thicker in the middle; **converges** light; used as a **magnifying glass**, in cameras and to correct **long sight (hypermetropia)**.
**Concave (diverging) lens** — thinner in the middle; **diverges** light; gives a small virtual image; corrects **short sight (myopia)**.
A convex lens can focus sunlight to a point and **burn paper**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Laws of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection; plane mirror image = virtual, erect, laterally inverted.
Convex mirror = diverging (rear-view, wide view; small virtual erect image).
Convex lens = converging (magnifying glass, camera); concave lens = diverging.
Convex lens corrects long sight; concave lens corrects short sight.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **convex mirror** always gives a **small, virtual, erect** image (rear-view mirror).
A **concave mirror** is used in **headlights/torches** and as a **shaving** mirror.
